account.identity.label: Account and sessions
account.identity.about: Read account settings and end sign-in sessions.
account.identity.core: People must be able to view their account and sign out.

account.identity_sync.label: Account sync with WorkOS
account.identity_sync.about: Accept signed WorkOS events that keep emails, revoked sessions and deleted accounts in step.
account.identity_sync.core: Revoked sessions, password resets and deleted users must reach Selecta at once.

account.labs.label: Labs
account.labs.about: Opt into preview features that your plan is allowed to use.

account.deletion.label: Account deletion
account.deletion.about: Request account removal and revoke active sessions.
account.deletion.core: People must always be able to request deletion of their account.

account.data_export.label: Account data export
account.data_export.about: Download a portable copy of available account data and original files.
account.data_export.core: People must be able to take a copy of their personal data.

account.lucy_settings.label: Lucy settings in Cloud
account.lucy_settings.about: Choose whether to use Lucy, its phases and what it may share; see this month's Lucy turns.

cloud.signups.label: New accounts
cloud.signups.about: Allow new Cloud users to complete account onboarding.

cloud.hosted_media.label: Cloud library
cloud.hosted_media.about: The umbrella grant for uploading and processing audio in Cloud (ADR-0456). The build ships on so a rule can grant it, and with no matching rule it is off: music on the member's devices is the default and a cloud library is a staff grant (ADR-0455).

cloud.uploads.label: Cloud uploads
cloud.uploads.about: Upload private audio files to a Cloud workspace.

storage.upload_identity.label: Uploads join the song they are for
storage.upload_identity.about: Uploading a song that is already in your library adds the file to that same song, matched by its file, an older copy of it or its audio, so its measurements, corrections, mixes and ratings stay with it; an unsure match becomes another version of the song. Also adds a check that says what a batch of uploads would do before anything is sent. Off: an upload finds its song by the exact file only, as before.
storage.upload_identity.cloud_surface_reason: Song identity and a dry run underneath uploads; it adds no page or control of its own.

cloud.move_to_cloud.label: Upload songs from this device
cloud.move_to_cloud.about: A member with a cloud library can upload songs from this device to it, one song at a time, carrying on after a reload or a closed tab, and then play them from the cloud library only: the song leaves this device's list, the file on this device stays exactly as it is, folder checks never add it back, and each song can play from this device again. The build ships it on; an account without the cloud library still sees nothing, because it needs the cloud library grant, uploads and uploads joining their song. Off, nothing about it is shown.

cloud.stored_media.label: Stored media
cloud.stored_media.about: List, play, export and delete audio already stored in Cloud. Reads of stored media stay open without the cloud library grant, so nobody's library goes dark (ADR-0456).

cloud.hosted_render.label: Cloud studio
cloud.hosted_render.about: For an account with a cloud library, the cloud studio runs the Desktop app's engine on uploaded songs: analysis at upload, the Desktop planner's order, rendered transitions placed the Desktop app's way, a lossless playback file per song and a rendered export (selecta.hosted_render). Off: uploads are stored and play as before, unprocessed.

cloud.hosted_brain.label: Uploaded-music mixes from SelectaDJ's own planner
cloud.hosted_brain.about: For an account with a cloud library, a server mix of uploaded songs is ordered and each transition chosen by the same planner the Desktop app uses (selecta.hosted_brain, workers.engine_core): the songs' measurements come from the account's song facts, every way into the next song is weighed and ranked, and each transition is rendered, checked and repaired by the Desktop's own rule, at most five takes and a clean cut. Off: the older order and move choice, exactly as before. Off until it has been listened to.
cloud.hosted_brain.cloud_surface_reason: Changes which transitions the server renders for a cloud library mix, not any screen: the cloud library card looks and works the same either way

cloud.local_first.label: Music on the member's devices
cloud.local_first.about: Selects the navigation and browser-owned playback for music on the member's devices in personal Cloud; the legacy pages remain when off (ADR-0455).

cloud.workspace.label: Browser Workspace
cloud.workspace.about: Workspace for music on this device: an overview of the library and what this browser is doing in the background, the interface choices, connecting music, this browser's storage and a browser diagnostics panel. Analysis and learning stay on a computer running SelectaDJ. When off, the device cards stay in More as This device.

cloud.resilient_import.label: Import that survives interruptions
cloud.resilient_import.about: A durable import journal in this browser: it retries, waits for the connection, and carries on after a reload or sign-in without re-reading finished files.

cloud.music_folders.label: Your music folders, watched
cloud.music_folders.about: The member can connect several music folders on this device. Each is listed with its song count, when it was last checked and whether the browser still allows it; folders the browser still allows are checked for new, changed and missing songs when SelectaDJ opens and when the tab comes back. Folder names and handles stay in this browser; nothing about a folder goes to the server. Off, one folder is remembered only to carry on an interrupted import, as before.

cloud.offline_shell.label: Cloud opens offline
cloud.offline_shell.about: The app opens without a connection and the library shows what this device already knows.

cloud.offline_playback.label: Playback through a dropped connection
cloud.offline_playback.about: A playing device keeps playing its own files while the connection is down and settles the playback lease when it returns.

cloud.mix_outbox.label: Mix changes wait for the connection
cloud.mix_outbox.about: Mixes made or edited offline are kept in this browser and sent when the connection returns.

cloud.hosted_shell.label: Cloud library pages on the shared shell
cloud.hosted_shell.about: Draws the cloud library pages (overview, Listen, Make a Mix, Library and the account places in More) inside the same shell as music on the member's devices; the legacy side rail remains when off.

cloud.page_layout.label: Cloud pages fill the frame
cloud.page_layout.about: Every Cloud page uses the full width of the frame, with text kept to a readable line length; account, billing and onboarding pages stay narrow and centred; Add music shows its storage beside the uploads on wide screens. Notices above the page show one at a time, with the rest folded into one line. Off, pages are drawn as before.

cloud.one_mixer.label: One Make a Mix for songs in both places
cloud.one_mixer.about: For an account with songs on its devices and in its cloud library, Make a Mix is the same mixer everyone has: the mix it makes becomes the current mix, so Listen, the editor, My Mixes and the mini player follow it, and Listen says when transitions are being got ready without holding up the music. Saving a mix as a file takes songs from both places, reading cloud songs to this device only; songs only on another device are left out by name. When every song is in the cloud library, the file can also be made there. Off: such an account keeps its separate cloud library card, and a file is saved only from songs on this device.

cloud.catalogue_play.label: Phones and other devices play cloud songs
cloud.catalogue_play.about: A song in your cloud library plays on any device you are signed in on: it is found by the song itself, never by this device's own files or by its name, and its link is signed again when it runs out. Choosing where the music plays counts those songs as on every signed-in device, so a phone with no music of its own can play them here. Off, songs in the cloud library are matched as before.

cloud.progressive_import.label: Import continues in the background
cloud.progressive_import.about: A folder import keeps running while the member moves on: onboarding unlocks as songs land, a shell chip shows progress, and an interrupted import offers to carry on (ADR-0463 BF-0463-02).

cloud.content_cache.label: Reuse work on the same song by fingerprint
cloud.content_cache.about: Derived data on this device is keyed by the song's content hash, computed here from the file itself, so the same file under another account or another title reuses it: cached song bytes, and a device-wide store of tonal profiles, waveforms and durations, with a fingerprint memo so a folder imported here before is not read in full again (ADR-0469 amendment). Off, everything is keyed per workspace, every import hashes every file, and nothing is shared.

cloud.hosted_dedupe.label: Share machine-derived data across accounts by fingerprint
cloud.hosted_dedupe.about: Server side of ADR-0469: deterministic derivations of an uploaded file's bytes may be reused by another workspace that holds the same bytes as a server-hashed upload; titles, ratings and history never join, and a client-claimed hash grants nothing. Off, every workspace keeps its own derived data as before.

cloud.local_first_labs.label: Labs: music on your devices
cloud.local_first_labs.about: Lets a beta cohort opt into music on their devices themselves, give feedback and opt out again; opting in adds the member to a cloud.local_first targeting rule (ADR-0467 step 3).

cloud.brain.label: Planning from song facts
cloud.brain.about: SelectaDJ's planner runs in Cloud from the facts a member's device measured for their songs (ADR-0479, docs/engineering/cloud-planning.md): a device saves a song's measurements (tempo, beats and bars, sections, key, loudness, per-bar energy and tone numbers; never audio or paths) and the member's tempo and key corrections, and Cloud answers with the ranked transitions between two songs and their scripts, the repair rule's next step, a mix's order and the idea cards. A device reports each seam it rendered (the pair, the option, the audit's verdict, who rendered it, the clip's length and hash; never the clip), any device can see which seams exist for a pair, and the member's Good and Bad on them (POST /api/seams/{key}/rate, GET /api/memory/ratings, which also need this flag) teach the planner. With cloud.account_mixes, the Desktop's mix and draft routes answer for the account too. Off: these routes answer flag_off and nothing is saved or planned.
cloud.brain.cloud_surface_reason: Routes a device and a studio call; with cloud.device_analysis on, the browser sends its measurements and plays the planner's order and transitions, which changes no screen

cloud.account_mixes.label: Your mixes in one place
cloud.account_mixes.about: The account's mixes come from one place on every device: the current mix and every draft are kept with the account in the same form the Desktop app keeps them (ADR-0479, docs/engineering/engine-store-mixes.md), and the browser reads and changes them through the Desktop's own mix routes, which also need cloud.brain. The account's song requests are kept with it the same way and answer the Desktop's request routes, since a request joins the account's mix. The first time an account uses them, its saved browser mixes are copied in as drafts once; nothing about them is changed or removed. Mixes hold catalogue song ids and transition choices, never audio or file paths. Off until it has been tried on a real account: the browser keeps its saved browser mixes as before, and these routes answer flag_off.
cloud.account_mixes.cloud_surface_reason: Changes where the browser keeps a mix, not any screen: Make a Mix, the editor and My Mixes look and work the same either way

cloud.local_media.label: Local media catalogue
cloud.local_media.about: The metadata-only catalogue of songs on the member's own devices; no audio is uploaded (ADR-0458).

billing.checkout.label: Plan checkout
billing.checkout.about: Start or change a paid Selecta Cloud subscription.

billing.portal.label: Subscription portal
billing.portal.about: Manage or cancel an existing paid Selecta Cloud subscription.

account.workspace_name.label: Workspace name
account.workspace_name.about: Rename the personal workspace from its starting name, offered once on Workspace.

account.new_device_email.label: New device email
account.new_device_email.about: Email the person once when a new device signs in to their account, with a way to sign out everywhere.
account.new_device_email.cloud_surface_reason: An email sent by the maintenance task; nothing on a Cloud screen changes

cloud.rate_limits.label: API rate limits
cloud.rate_limits.about: Per-account and per-IP request limits in the Cloud API, with stricter limits for checkout, account changes, search and upload plans.
cloud.rate_limits.cloud_surface_reason: A request limit has no screen; a refused request says why and when to try again

cloud.idempotency.label: Replayed writes
cloud.idempotency.about: A Cloud write sent again with the same Idempotency-Key within 24 hours gets the first answer back instead of doing it twice.
cloud.idempotency.cloud_surface_reason: Replaying a stored answer has no screen; the person simply never sees a double

billing.standing.label: Billing notices and emails
billing.standing.about: Tell the customer when a payment failed, needs confirming, or a plan is ending or has ended, in the app and by email.
words: Update your card to keep it

cloud.operations.label: Cloud operations
cloud.operations.about: Schema migrations, the worker gateway, and the maintenance and recovery commands that keep the service correct.
cloud.operations.core: The cloud service can't run, recover or erase data on time without them.

cloud.tracing.label: Job tracing
cloud.tracing.about: OpenTelemetry spans across the API, worker gateway, workers and storage, one trace per job with its id as a span attribute.

cloud.metrics.label: Service metrics
cloud.metrics.about: OpenTelemetry metrics the SLOs and alerts read: lost jobs, webhook-to-entitlement time, queue age, quarantines, spend ceilings, audit writes, reconciliation drift, backups and the maintenance leader.

cloud.error_reporting.label: Error reporting
cloud.error_reporting.about: Send API, gateway, maintenance and worker errors to Sentry, scrubbed of signed links, tokens and email addresses. Needs SELECTA_SENTRY_DSN; nothing is sent without it.

cloud.email.label: Transactional email
cloud.email.about: Email people from SelectaDJ when a long job finishes or their storage goes over quota, through Postmark or Resend. Needs the SELECTA_EMAIL_* settings on the maintenance service.

cloud.export_expiry.label: Export expiry
cloud.export_expiry.about: The maintenance leader deletes finished exports when their plan's retention runs out (Free 7 days, Standard 30, Premium 90) and gives their bytes back to the quota.

cloud.hosted_caps.label: Cloud studio daily caps
cloud.hosted_caps.about: A cloud library account's first analysis of a song takes one of the plan's daily song analyses, and each new transition takes its measured seconds from the plan's daily transition time (selecta.hosted_caps). Off: nothing is counted or refused.

cloud.derived_gc.label: Derived files collector
cloud.derived_gc.about: The maintenance leader deletes derived files no artifact row or live job names, from attempts that ended over 6 hours ago, and playback files unused for 30 days (storage.derived_gc). Off: the task runs dry and only reports, so an operator can read `selecta storage gc` first.

cloud.operator_alerts.label: Operator alert email
cloud.operator_alerts.about: The maintenance leader emails SELECTA_ALERT_EMAIL when queued work is stuck, the worker gateway stops answering, the autoscaler fails or a pool reaches its daily spend ceiling: once an hour at most, and once when it clears (notify.operator_alerts).

cloud.autoscale.label: Worker autoscaling
cloud.autoscale.about: The maintenance leader sizes each worker pool from the queue and asks the configured launcher (Modal) to start or stop workers.

cloud.dmca_renewal_reminder.label: DMCA agent renewal reminder
cloud.dmca_renewal_reminder.about: The maintenance leader raises an owner alert from 90 days before the DMCA designated agent's three-year registration lapses, and daily once it has.

cloud.privacy_notice_draft.label: Privacy notice draft
cloud.privacy_notice_draft.about: Shows the draft privacy notice, marked as a draft pending legal review, under Settings so the owner and a privacy adviser can read it in place. Off by default: it is not published.

cloud.device_check.label: Device check
cloud.device_check.about: A checklist under Settings for the real-device checks (Play here, an offline speaker, the iPhone screen-on note, seam alignment) that reads what this browser supports and writes a copyable record. Off by default.

billing.webhooks.label: Billing updates
billing.webhooks.about: Accept signed subscription state changes from Stripe.
billing.webhooks.core: Billing changes must be applied even when checkout is paused.

devices.label: Playback devices
devices.about: Sign browsers in as devices, list, rename and sign them out, and move playback between them with Play here.

devices.remote_control.label: Remote playback control
devices.remote_control.about: Control the account's active playback session from another device.

devices.browser_player.label: Browser player
devices.browser_player.about: The in-browser audio engine registered as a playback device (ADR-0457).

cloud.browser_dsp.label: Browser DSP
cloud.browser_dsp.about: The browser player's mixing DSP tiers, labelled honestly where they differ musically (ADR-0459).

cloud.seam_lead.label: Browser transitions planned early
cloud.seam_lead.about: In a browser mix, each transition is worked out as its song starts instead of 45 seconds before it ends, every song plays at one level (-14 LUFS, as on Desktop), and a slow analysis moment is waited for instead of turning beatmatching off for the visit (ADR-0479 phase 1). Off: transitions are planned late and songs play at their own level, as before.

cloud.browser_moves.label: Browser transition moves
cloud.browser_moves.about: The Desktop app's moves in a browser mix: SelectaDJ picks a bass swap, filter sweep, cut, echo out or reverb wash for each transition from the audio as it plays, the member can choose one, and each transition says what really played (ADR-0459).

cloud.browser_harmonic.label: Browser harmonic matches
cloud.browser_harmonic.about: Make a Mix's Harmonic matches in a browser library: each song this device can play gets a whole-song key profile measured here in spare time, songs whose profiles and keys line up are offered as pairs to hear, and the audition plays the end of one into the start of the other from the files on this device. It is not the Desktop app's bar-by-bar chord search.

cloud.device_analysis.label: Whole-song facts measured on this device
cloud.device_analysis.about: In a browser library, the background measuring that makes key profiles also measures each song whole, the way the Desktop does: its beat grid, bars, energy, chroma, tone, key, sections and loudness, kept in this browser. With cloud.brain also on, those numbers (never audio, paths or file names) are saved to the account, and the account's planner orders new browser mixes and chooses each transition from them (docs/engineering/device-to-account.md). Beats come from the Desktop's own tracker, Beat This, run in the browser where its model file is served from SelectaDJ's site, its Tier 3 review has passed and the device is fast enough; elsewhere from a lighter estimate, which the account ranks below the tracker and measures again once the tracker is there (docs/engineering/device-beats.md). Off by default while the owner publishes the model file and signs the review. Off: songs get their key profile only, nothing is sent, and mixes are ordered and blended as before.
cloud.device_analysis.cloud_surface_reason: Measured and sent in the background; it changes the order and transitions of browser mixes, not any screen

cloud.device_render.label: Transitions rendered on this device
cloud.device_render.about: The browser's own rendering of transitions: it plays each transition the account's planner describes into a short clip ahead of time, the way the Desktop does, measures it with the Desktop's checks and follows the Desktop's repair rule (docs/engineering/device-render.md). With it on, with cloud.brain on and both songs measured, a playing mix prepares its next two transitions this way and plays each finished clip between the two songs, keeping clips on this device; a transition not ready in time, or in any doubt, plays live as before (docs/engineering/device-studio-playback.md). The Listening Room then compares the planner's choice made ahead with the other two ways. Its time-stretch is the browser's own, not the Desktop's Rubber Band. Off: no transition is rendered on this device and mixes blend live as before.
cloud.device_render.cloud_surface_reason: Renders in a background worker and changes how transitions sound, not any screen; the Listening Room's comparison is behind its own flag

cloud.browser_stems.label: Browser stem moves
cloud.browser_stems.about: Splitting songs into voice, drums, bass and melody on this device, only around each transition, for vocal ride, strip and land and intertwined stems in browser mixes (ADR-0459 Tier 3). Each device reports unsupported until the stem model's licence review and that device's evidence record pass.

cloud.venue_tablet.label: Venue tablet posture
cloud.venue_tablet.about: The single-tablet venue posture: capability checks and readiness guidance for a browser device playing a venue (ADR-0460).

cloud.local_export.label: Local export
cloud.local_export.about: Render a mix to a file in the browser player and save it on the member's own device; nothing is uploaded.

rooms.label: Rooms
rooms.about: Let Premium hosts share a request room with guests.

rooms.votes.label: Room votes
rooms.votes.about: Let room guests vote on song requests.

rooms.display.label: Room display
rooms.display.about: Pair a screen to show the room QR code and playback queue.

rooms.keeps.label: Keep the songs you liked
rooms.keeps.about: A room guest's heart saves the playing song to a list kept only on their own phone.

rooms.reactions.label: Room reactions
rooms.reactions.about: Guests love the playing song or the blend into it; the room sees counts, and the planner learns what rooms loved.

rooms.rounds.label: Pick the next song
rooms.rounds.about: The room votes between songs the DJ can blend into, and the winner goes into the mix.

rooms.dedications.label: Room dedications
rooms.dedications.about: A guest adds one line from a fixed list to their own request, shown while the song plays.

rooms.recap.label: Tonight in numbers
rooms.recap.about: When a room ends, the host, its guests and a paired screen see the room's totals.

rooms.cloud_songs.label: Rooms offer songs in your cloud library
rooms.cloud_songs.about: For an account with a cloud library, a room also offers the songs in it, because the device playing the room can play them from there; any signed-in device can then play the room. Songs kept only on another device stay out, as before. Off, a room offers only the songs on the device playing it.

lucy.deep_plan.label: Lucy deep planning
lucy.deep_plan.about: Use Lucy's premium planning model and larger plan allowance.

admin.console.label: Staff console
admin.console.about: Show internal tools to authenticated staff with the required permission.

admin.workers.label: Staff console: Workers
admin.workers.about: The staff console's Workers page: the cloud studio at a glance per pool, the gateway, autoscaler, storage and flags around the workers, customer waits, processing cost against a budget, and guarded actions (retry, cancel long waits, pause a pool, ask the autoscaler for a worker).
